newsitem.title: GERMANY: Focus-German Postbank mulls links with DSL.
newsitem.headline: Focus-German Postbank mulls links with DSL.

text.p: In the latest sign of consolidation in the overcrowded German banking sector, the soon-to-be privatised postal bank Postbank AG on Wednesday confirmed it was discussing links with fellow state-owned bank DSL Bank.
DSL separately announced that the diversified financial services company BHW had reduced its DSL stake to just above 10 percent from more than 20 percent. It made no further comment.

A Postbank spokesman, responding to earlier queries, said the bank had been discussing co-operation with DSL (Deutsche Siedlungs und Landesrentenbank) for some time. DSL's former chief executive, Dieter Boening, took over as chief of Postbank on July 1.
But Postbank's spokesman declined to comment on a media report that the bank, which has a strong position in the retail segment, was poised for an outright takeover of DSL.

In an article released ahead of publication, the Wirtschaftswoche magazine said that Postbank planned to take over DSL in a transaction due to be completed by the start of 1998, ahead of Postbank's planned privatisation next summer.
Such a deal would be fully in keeping with the consolidation trend that has sent the German banking sector into turmoil in the past year.

In the commercial banking sector, the largest move to date was last month's plans for a mega-merger between the Bavarian mortgage giants Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel-Bank AG, creating Germany's second largest commercial bank by assets.
